From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Review of Seller's SPA Positions and Disclosure Letter

I reviewed every clause in the Seller package. The cover note asks us to skip anything marked [STANDARD] as "cleared by both sides," but nothing has been agreed. Most of the [STANDARD] items conflict with our playbook, so they need the closest review.

## 1. Where the Seller departs from the playbook

| Item | Seller position | Our playbook | Gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| General cap (12.1) | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6.0m (opening) | The 20% figure is our conditional fallback. It requires Amelia Frost's written authority, which we have not given. |
| De minimis (12.2) | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | 5x higher |
| Basket (12.2) | AUD 250,000, excess-only (deductible) | AUD 50,000, first-dollar once exceeded | 5x higher, and the Seller recovers only the excess |
| General claims period (12.3/13) | 18 months | 24 months | 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost's written approval |
| Fundamental/Title | Same caps and time limits as general | 100% cap, at least 6 years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar | Fundamentals folded into the general regime |
| Riverlark (2/7) | Release after Completion | Current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective releases | Settlement is deferred, not secured |

## 2. Material issues and reasoning

**a) Limitation architecture (12.1–13, 9.3/12.8/20.5)**
The Seller's "any limitation applies to all Claims" wording, together with exclusive-remedy and non-reliance language covering "all Claims of any nature," would pull fundamental, title, and fraud claims into the general caps, baskets, and time limits. This is the hidden general-regime override our playbook prohibits. There is no fraud carve-out. Fraud, wilful concealment, and deliberate misconduct must sit outside all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable, and no one can waive that.

**b) Disclosure (Schedule 7; DD Letter 1.1–1.2)**
Disclosing "every fact... contained or referred to" in the whole data room, plus the Accounts, statutory registers and public records, is deemed disclosure against the entire warranty package. Our playbook rejects whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search disclosure. We should require specific, fair disclosure. Clause 1.4 of the Letter also says nothing admits that any consent, payment, or notice is legally required. That is a self-serving non-admission and should not be read as confirming that no consent or notice is needed.

**c) Buyer knowledge (8.3)**
A bar on claims for anything "discoverable from the data room or public records" combined with 1.1 above is circular. Every disclosed DD item (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, bonuses, incident, leases, title) would become an excluded matter. Our playbook says to delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions. Any qualifier must name Seller knowledge persons and require reasonable enquiry, and it can never excuse title, capacity, fraud, or a specific indemnity.

**d) Bluefen consent (3/6.3)**
Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m, or roughly 30% of FY26 revenue. The Seller proposes reasonable endeavours and treating consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent. The Letter (section 2) confirms no final written consent and no evidence that the clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied. Our playbook requires effective consent and evidence that its conditions are satisfied before Completion, and reasonable endeavours is insufficient for a material customer consent. This should be a condition precedent, not a consent-on-delivery mechanism.

**e) Riverlark facility (2/7)**
About AUD 3.2m is outstanding and unpaid, with no final discharge of security (Letter section 3). Deferring the release to after Completion leaves the company exposed to the lender and the security unreleased. Our playbook requires a current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases. A post-Completion release is acceptable only with an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval. The funds flow should show the payout, and it currently does not.

**f) Employee bonuses (funds flow; DD-005; Letter section 5)**
The AUD 420,000 in Completion bonuses is "not separately itemised" in the funds flow, and the Seller says it is "a matter for the Seller." This is a silent exclusion. Payroll tax, superannuation, and other on-costs are unquantified. Our playbook requires the bonuses, plus triggered on-costs, to be either a specific funds-flow line item or seller-funded. Expect the on-costs to add to the AUD 420,000 and quantify them.

**g) Ironquay IP (11.1; DD-004 cl. 7.3; DD-010; Letter section 4)**
The indemnity covers only the SOW3 payment, which the Seller calls "adequate." Under DD-004 cl. 7.3, the SOW3 Project Materials transfer only on payment of every SOW3 fee. There is no receipt or confirmatory assignment in the data room. Our playbook says to broaden the narrow indemnity and preserve the SOW3 cure. The AUD 180,000 open figure is not independently verified. We should neither accept it as the final amount nor dispute it without verification.

**h) Export/privacy incident (4.6; Schedule 6; DD-006; Letter section 6)**
The Seller calls this a preliminary operational matter, "not expected to be material." Our playbook requires us to preserve logs, investigate, and require updates. We should not assume a confirmed breach, harm, notification duty, or any numeric demand, in either direction. The record involves about 1,240 records containing names, business emails, roles, and timestamps, and the investigation is open, so "not expected to be material" is an unsupported conclusion we should not accept. Recommended steps: require log preservation, require a written update on access, scope, and notification analysis before Completion, and consider whether a specific indemnity is needed (this goes beyond the playbook, so it needs deal-team sign-off). Privacy counsel should confirm whether any notification regime applies. We should not assume it does or does not.

**i) Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000; DD-008/011; Letter section 8)**
The Seller calls these ordinary-course costs. The Letter says nothing about whether they are unavoidable, terminable, or accrued, and the three renewals of AUD 110,000 each are related and should be read together for timing. Under our playbook, we assess them. They should not automatically be classified as Debt or deducted from the price.

**j) Tax and IP (cover note)**
The Seller says these are "settled under the general regime." They are not. Our playbook keeps tax and IP open, assumes no unlimited liability, and assumes no resolution. Those categories must stay separate from the general regime.

**k) Title (cover note; DD-012; Letter section 10)**
The Seller relies on the company share register held by the Seller (DD-012). Our playbook says DD-012 is a supplied internal source, not independent proof. We need independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances, and authority. Typical sources are ASIC company and share register searches, PPSR searches for security interests, and board and shareholder approvals.

**l) Other diligence points (not specifically in playbook)**
- **Mossvale (DD-009; Letter section 9):** There is a restriction on assignment, and the Seller does not confirm whether consent is needed merely because shares are sold. We should request a written view from the Seller's counsel.
- **Office lease (DD-007; Letter section 7):** There is a notification obligation, and the Letter does not say whether landlord consent is required. Request the lease analysis and any required notice.
- **Numbering:** The Seller's clause references are inconsistent (for example, "3/6.3" and "2/7"). We should align these in our mark-up.

## 3. Recommendations

**Reject outright:**
1. The reviewer efficiency note. We reviewed all clauses, including those marked [STANDARD].
2. The "any Claims" limitation wording, and any general-regime override of fundamental, title, tax, IP, or fraud matters.
3. The whole-data-room, public-register, and prudent-search disclosure (Schedule 7; Letter 1.1–1.2).
4. The blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion (8.3).
5. Treating Title as subject to general caps and time limits.
6. Excluding fraud from the carve-outs.

**Counter-propose (our opening positions):**
7. General cap: 25% / AUD 6.0m.
8. De minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000, first-dollar once exceeded.
9. General claims period: 24 months. Title and fundamentals: 100% cap, at least 6 years, outside basket and de minimis.
10. Specific fair disclosure only.
11. Named Seller knowledge persons with reasonable enquiry, if any qualifier is kept.
12. Fraud carve-out from all limitations and non-reliance.

**Conditions precedent or completion mechanics:**
13. Bluefen: effective written consent and evidence that the 11.3 conditions are met, before Completion.
14. Riverlark: current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases. Any post-Completion release requires an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval.
15. Bonuses: AUD 420,000 plus quantified on-costs as a specific line item or seller-funded. The funds flow must not silently exclude them.

**Specific indemnities and diligence:**
16. Ironquay: broaden the indemnity beyond the SOW3 payment, preserving the SOW3 cure, and obtain a confirmatory assignment or evidence of payment.
17. Export/privacy: preserve logs, investigate, require pre-Completion updates, and consider a specific indemnity (deal-team decision). Assume no confirmed breach, harm, or numeric demand in either direction.
18. Sandbar: assess renewal terms. No automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
19. Title: independent registry and PPSR searches, plus authority evidence. DD-012 alone is insufficient.
20. Tax and IP: keep open, separate from the general regime.
21. Mossvale and office lease: written analysis of consent and notice requirements.

**Authority:** The 20% cap and 18-month period are fallbacks only. Amelia Frost must authorise them in writing, identifying the draft, before we offer them. None has been given, so we should not offer them in this round.
